name: kinesic_amnesia_glyphs
label: Whispers of Forgotten Movement
godotFeature: AnimationTree, GDScript (input parsing, dynamic animation blending, signal handling)
poeticVision: Imagine Lyra, mid-leap across a collapsing memory, her body suddenly forgetting the precise sequence of muscle contractions for a perfect landing. A ghost of the *correct* movement flickers at the edge of your vision — a spectral echo of mastery. You feel the frantic effort to recall, your fingers twitching on the controller, trying to force her muscles into the forgotten pattern. Each stumble, each almost-fall, is a chilling reminder: your very ability to *move* is tied to your identity, and forgetting is taking away your physical competence. It's the silent scream of a body betraying its self, forcing you to re-learn, mid-chase, what you once knew instinctively.
usage:
Attach this `kinesic_amnesia_manager.gd` script to a Node in your scene (e.g., as a child of your Player node, or as an Autoload singleton). Configure the `animation_tree_path` export variable to point to your player's AnimationTree node. Ensure your Godot Project Settings Input Map defines the `input_actions` (e.g., 'ui_up', 'ui_down', 'ui_left', 'ui_right').

Your player's movement controller script should call `kinesic_amnesia_manager.attempt_complex_movement("action_name")` before executing any complex movement (e.g., a high jump, a specific dodge). If this function returns `true`, the movement should be interrupted, and the manager will handle the amnesia event, blending the animation to a 'decayed' state.

A separate UI script should connect to the `challenge_started`, `challenge_input_required`, and `challenge_completed` signals to display the input challenge to the player and react to its outcome. The `AnimationTree` should have a `BlendSpace1D` with a parameter (e.g., `parameters/KinesicBlend/blend_position`) that blends between a 'mastered' animation (value 0.0) and a 'decayed' or 'stumble' animation (value 1.0) for the affected movement.

parameters.name: animation_tree_path
parameters.description: The NodePath to the AnimationTree node that controls Lyra's animations. This is used to dynamically blend between 'mastered' and 'decayed' movement animations.

parameters.name: amnesia_threshold
parameters.description: The minimum 'amnesia_chance' (derived from _kinesic_memory_index) required for an amnesia event to potentially trigger. A higher value makes amnesia more likely at higher memory indices.

parameters.name: challenge_duration
parameters.description: The time in seconds the player has to complete the input sequence challenge before it automatically fails.

parameters.name: min_challenge_length
parameters.description: The minimum number of input actions in a procedurally generated challenge sequence.

parameters.name: max_challenge_length
parameters.description: The maximum number of input actions in a procedurally generated challenge sequence.

parameters.name: input_actions
parameters.description: A list of Godot InputMap action names that can be used as inputs in the challenge sequence. These actions must be defined in your Project Settings -> Input Map.

verdict: In the frantic dance of forgetting, Lyra's body becomes a battleground where muscle memory is the last, desperate whisper of who she once was.
impact: This mechanic will profoundly deepen the player's connection to Lyra's struggle, transforming abstract identity loss into a tangible, moment-to-moment fight for physical competence. Every stumble becomes a chilling reminder of her fading self, forcing players to viscerally experience the 'grief of self-loss' as they frantically re-learn basic movements under the relentless pressure of the Silence. It elevates the core theme of identity erosion from narrative to direct, urgent gameplay.
